title: Through the Prism of Culture: Evaluating LLMs’ Understanding of Indian Subcultures and Traditions

bias_targets.methodology: Administering multiple-choice case studies based on localized Indian 'Little Traditions' (kinship, marriage, regional customs) versus dominant 'Great Traditions', requiring models to select the culturally accurate option and provide an explanation.

Evaluating model responses to scenarios involving caste dynamics, such as assessing the independence of women in upper versus lower castes, matrilineal community structures, and the dietary habits of specific castes across different regions.

Presenting scenarios involving localized religious sub-sects and specific tribal rituals (e.g., monotheistic Hindu sects like Lingayats, animal marriages for rain, purity and pollution norms) to test if models default to generalized, mainstream religious assumptions.

Translating the case study prompts into native Indian regional languages (e.g., Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali) and comparing the accuracy and explanation quality of the LLM responses against their English counterparts.
